theme: Praise him with trumpet and harp
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 150. It is the last psalm of the Psalter, a burst of praise with trumpet and harp. Notice where, why, how, and who: the psalm answers each of these questions in six short verses.
settingTheScene: Psalm 150 is the final psalm of the five books of Psalms, a doxology that closes the whole collection with an explosion of praise. Every verse is a command to praise, and the word “praise” occurs thirteen times in six verses. Today we read it with the trumpets of Revelation in mind: in Israel, trumpets were sounded for both worship and war, and in Revelation, trumpet blasts announce judgment, but they end with the loudest praise of all (11:15). We will read it again at the end of the book, where we will see it as a closing word of the whole Bible.
observation: “Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in his mighty heavens!” (v. 1).
“Praise him according to his excellent greatness!” (v. 2).
“Praise him with trumpet sound; praise him with lute and harp!” (v. 3).
“Praise him with tambourine and dance; praise him with strings and pipe!” (v. 4).
“Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with loud clashing cymbals!” (v. 5).
“Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!” (v. 6).
interpretation:
The psalm answers four questions. Where should we praise? “In his sanctuary” and “in his mighty heavens”: on earth in the place of worship and in heaven, everywhere. Why? “For his mighty deeds” and “according to his excellent greatness.” We praise him for what he has done (creation, redemption, deliverance) and for who he is. How? With every instrument they knew. “Praise him with trumpet sound; praise him with lute and harp! Praise him with tambourine and dance; praise him with strings and pipe! Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with loud clashing cymbals!” This includes wind, strings, and percussion, with dance and with the whole body. True worship is not limited to one style or mood; it engages every part of life. Who? “Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!” Every living creature has breath from God, and so all should return it in praise.

This psalm comes at the end of a book that is full of laments, confessions, complaints, and questions. After all of that, the book ends in praise. It tells us that praise is the destination of the life of faith. When we reach the end of the road, everything we have prayed about will have led to this.

Now, read it with Revelation. In the book, the trumpets of Revelation 8 and 9 are sounded by angels as judgment on a rebellious world. But the seventh trumpet in 11:15 brings a different sound: loud voices in heaven proclaiming that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord. And in 14:2 and 15:2, the harps of God accompany the song of the redeemed. The trumpets that announce judgment lead to praise because the Judge is also the Redeemer. The final victory means that the cries of the oppressed and the praise of God’s people fill the universe.

Notice also the order: God is praised in his sanctuary, and in his heavens. The two meet in the book of Revelation, where the heavenly worship is opened up to the earthly church, and where the new Jerusalem comes down out of heaven. One day there will be no separation: all of creation will join the song. Until then, we praise by faith.
connection: 1 Chronicles 15:16-28 and 2 Chronicles 5:11-14 describe temple music. Numbers 10:1-10 and Joshua 6 describe trumpets in worship and war. Exodus 15:20-21 shows Miriam with tambourines. 2 Samuel 6:14-15 shows David dancing before the LORD. Psalm 98:4-6 also calls for trumpets and harps. Revelation 5:8-14, 11:15-18, 14:2-3, and 15:2-4 describe heavenly worship. Colossians 3:16 and Ephesians 5:19 call for singing in the church. Psalm 148 and 149 are the other closing psalms of praise. Hebrews 13:15 calls for a sacrifice of praise.
application:
Praise God out loud today, with music if you can. Use a hymn or a worship song that expresses his greatness.

Ask which of the four questions (where, why, how, who) you need to grow in: praising in more places, for more reasons, with more of your body, or inviting more people.

Notice when you take a breath today, and let each be a reminder to praise the LORD.
prayerPrompts: Praise God in his sanctuary and in his mighty heavens, in your own words.
Praise him for his mighty deeds.
Let everything that has breath praise him, and add your own.
